name: BN6's battle a fight frame behind BN4's
fields: every record of BN6's battle, the same offset for all (tools/xdiff_bn4.py compare: the family's, MegaMan's and the world's objects, their AI and collision data, the panels, the run order, the sounds, the events and the family's draws), BN6's at t + 1 against BN4's at t; BN6's battle traced a fight frame longer and its keys by the timer taken a frame later (src/dev/xdiff.c, Side.behind), the family's own draws given BN4's of the frame before (rng=replay with lag=1, src/dev/xdiff_events.h xd_replay_lag). Every record a state drives, that is: what the battle's timer drives is compared at the same fight frame, its clock shown by its writer (bn4.clocks, bn4.sounds' clock). What still differs under the shift fails the spec (the family's) or keeps it INCONCLUSIVE (the world's), never a field or a role given a lag of its own; what is fixed before the first state keeps its own handling (BN6's per-frame RNG steps, not compared where the draws are replayed; BN6's MegaMan's companion, spawned by his init)
why: BN6's engine runs no state while the opening is paused, BN4's does, so BN6's whole battle runs a fight frame behind BN4's from the first state on. Both games' pause byte (BN4's [eToolkit+0x40]+9, BN6's [eToolkit+0x3C]+0xA) reads 1 from the appear to the fight, and each object runner (BN4 0x0800314C, BN6 0x080031AC) runs a paused object whose +0 has 0x04. BN4's state runner (0x08013C48) has no pause test and calls the state (0x08013D9A), so in the opening BN4's generic state 1 (0x0801013A) hands a virus its first own state and MegaMan's state 1 (0x08010A88) his ready 6, each run at the fight's first frame. BN6's (0x0801B1C4, from the virus dispatcher 0x0810A29C and MegaMan's update) tests the pause byte first (0x0800A03C, at 0x0801B1CC) and, for a CurAction not 0 whose flags (0x0801A166) have none of 0x40000100 and whose struck word (0x0801A180) has no 0x8000, returns at 0x0801B21A (b 0x0801B37A) without calling the state: BN6's state 1 (a virus's 0x080165B8, MegaMan's 0x08017888) runs at the fight's first frame and the first own state at the second (billy_v1: Billy's first own state at t1 in BN4 and t2 in BN6; MegaMan's ready setting his object's +0xB 4 and +0x20 9 at t1 in BN4, t2 in BN6, the same count-down to t10 and t11). Everything the states do follows a frame later: Billy's moves and reservations, its thunder striking MegaMan (t431 in BN4, t432 in BN6), the sounds they play. BN6's own Mettaur against BN4's starts the same way (game=bn4:bn6, foes=01@52). The lead's call (2026-11-04, the owner's to overturn): one offset for the whole battle, where the owner's earlier call (the port keeps BN6's timing) had it for the family alone. BN6's first fight frame, its states' 1, meets BN4's paused opening, which the trace does not keep, and is not compared
